channel.title: Insights Aggregator
channel.description: Investment insights from banks & asset managers, aggregated.

item.title: Global Data Pod Weekender: Tomayto, tomahto
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · Global Data Pod — The Federal Reserve joined the rate-hiking cycle this week with signals for further increases ahead. Global factors are contributing to what may become a more synchronized and larger international hiking cycle than previously anticipated, supported by strengthening cyclical momentum, though the outlook carries two-sided risks.

item.title: Flattish Markets and Highly Hawkish Hike (E277)
item.dc:creator: DoubleLine
item.description: DoubleLine · DoubleLine Minutes — Markets remained relatively flat during the week ended September 18th, with stocks experiencing a modest decline. The episode features analysis from DoubleLine experts discussing the implications of recent Federal Reserve policy decisions and market dynamics.

item.title: Trump-Xi Talks Put Trade and Tech in Focus
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — President Xi's upcoming White House visit on September 24th will focus on trade negotiations, rare earth minerals, and AI collaboration between the U.S. and China. The discussion follows Trump's May visit to Beijing, where both sides established frameworks for strategic stability and created new trade and investment dialogues. Key outcomes could affect supply chains, technology sector valuations, and broader market implications.

item.title: Global Rates & FX Views: The great central bank review
item.dc:creator: Bank of America
item.description: Bank of America · Global Research Unlocked — This discussion reviews recent decisions from the Federal Reserve, Bank of England, and Bank of Japan, with emphasis on the Fed's hawkish rate hike and its role in the broader global monetary tightening cycle. The panelists examine the resulting impacts on yield curves and currency markets across major economies. The session analyzes how these central bank actions are reshaping global rates and FX dynamics.

item.title: Signals & Noise: When Income Became an Outcome
item.dc:creator: Bank of America
item.description: Bank of America · Global Research Unlocked — Income investing has shifted from traditional bonds and dividends to derivatives-based strategies, with structured products and derivatives-linked ETFs gaining significant adoption. BofA Securities researchers examine why option-based income strategies remain attractive despite rising bond yields and how they integrate into diversified portfolios.

item.title: Global FX: Bullish beta, bullish USD reinforced
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · At Any Rate — JPMorgan's FX team discusses the outlook for currency markets following a week of significant G4 central bank decisions in mid-September 2026. The analysis reinforces bullish positioning for risk assets and the US dollar, reflecting broader market dynamics and monetary policy trajectories.

item.title: Global Commodities: The ways of water
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · At Any Rate — Middle East escalation and El Niño weather patterns are creating significant stress on global commodity markets, particularly affecting energy and agricultural sectors. The podcast examines how geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and Pacific Ocean climate conditions are driving price movements across commodity markets worldwide.

item.title: Global Data Pod: Western European central banks are on the move
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · Global Data Pod — Western European central banks are adopting a more hawkish policy stance, signaling a shift toward tighter monetary conditions. Greg Fuzesi and Allan Monks discuss the implications and drivers of this progressive change in Central Bank positioning across the region.

item.title: The yield rise goes global - Asset Class Insights
item.dc:creator: Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank · Deutsche Bank Wealth CIO Insights (web) — Global bond yields are rising amid a market repricing across fixed-income assets. Deutsche Bank's Wealth CIO explores the underlying drivers of this yield movement and identifies potential opportunities for fixed-income investors navigating the changing rate environment.

item.title: View from the markets: Déjà vu: What’s next for markets after the latest spike in oil prices? – EN
item.dc:creator: BNP Paribas
item.description: BNP Paribas · BNPP AM Viewpoint (web) — Oil prices have recently spiked, triggering a rise in global government bond yields and subsequent declines in equity markets. This market dynamic represents a recurring pattern, with similar episodes having occurred multiple times previously. Federal Reserve rate expectations have largely been priced into markets already.

item.title: The Week Ahead - A Double Header of Hikes
item.dc:creator: Nomura
item.description: Nomura · Nomura — The Week Ahead — Central banks are expected to deliver rate increases from the Fed and Bank of Japan this week, while European central banks including the Riksbank, Norges Bank, and SNB are anticipated to hold rates steady. Economic data points include rising core inflation in Singapore, rebounding job growth in Australia, and Bank Indonesia expected to maintain its current stance.

item.title: Under the Banyan Tree - AI: Debate, direction and Dutch disease
item.dc:creator: HSBC
item.description: HSBC · HSBC Global Viewpoint — HSBC's Head of AI and Data Science discusses artificial intelligence adoption trends, comparing approaches between China and the US, and examines calls from industry leaders for stricter AI regulation. The conversation covers the broader implications and strategic direction of AI development across different regions.

item.title: Understanding Liquid Alternatives
item.dc:creator: GMO
item.description: GMO · GMO Research Library & 7-Year Forecast (web) — GMO's asset allocation experts discuss how liquid alternative strategies offer diversification benefits, potential for alpha generation, and daily liquidity when incorporated into multi-asset portfolios. These vehicles provide investors with non-traditional exposure while maintaining accessibility compared to traditional alternatives.

item.title: 271: David Rubenstein, Co-Founder of The Carlyle Group, on the Business of Sports, Investing and Leadership
item.dc:creator: BlackRock
item.description: BlackRock · The Bid — David Rubenstein, co-founder of The Carlyle Group and owner of the Baltimore Orioles, discusses how sports investing has evolved as franchise valuations have increased and ownership has become more sophisticated. The conversation covers the unique economics of sports teams that blend financial returns with competitive outcomes, community impact, and fan engagement, along with emerging trends including media demand, analytics, and capital market developments influencing the sector.

item.title: Rich Friedman on the Rise of Private Markets and AI Investing
item.dc:creator: Goldman Sachs
item.description: Goldman Sachs · Goldman Sachs Exchanges — Rich Friedman, chairman of Goldman Sachs Asset Management, discusses the continued opportunities in private markets despite their significant growth, and shares his perspective that AI investment payoffs will materialize later than market expectations. He explains how principles developed over 45 years building the firm's merchant banking business inform his current investment approach.

item.title: India in focus
item.dc:creator: HSBC
item.description: HSBC · The Macro Brief — HSBC's Chief India Economist discusses key drivers of India's economic outlook, including growth resilience and efforts to enhance export competitiveness. The conversation covers macroeconomic factors shaping India's development trajectory and its position in global trade.

item.title: The Assets Powering the Next Investment Cycle
item.dc:creator: Man Group
item.description: Man Group · Man Institute Insights — This analysis examines the investment trends shaping the next market cycle, with a focus on essential assets and the case for investing in listed infrastructure. The discussion covers long-term structural shifts driving asset allocation and the role of infrastructure as a core holding in portfolios going forward.

item.title: Professor Alex Edmans, on the Madness of Markets… and Sustainable Investing
item.dc:creator: Man Group
item.description: Man Group · Man Institute Insights — Professor Alex Edmans from London Business School discusses behavioral patterns that lead intelligent investors to make irrational decisions and explores how market participants can identify and potentially capitalize on these psychological biases. The discussion covers the intersection of behavioral finance and sustainable investing practices.

item.title: Trends Matter, So Does Fed Credibility
item.dc:creator: Man Group
item.description: Man Group · Man Institute Insights — The Federal Reserve unanimously voted to raise interest rates for the first time in three years, signaling a shift in monetary policy stance. This rate hike reflects the Fed's response to inflation and changing economic conditions, with implications for market trends and central bank credibility.

item.title: The Opportunities for Investors amid Higher-for-Longer Interest Rates
item.dc:creator: Goldman Sachs
item.description: Goldman Sachs · GS Insights (web) — Goldman Sachs explores how elevated interest rates present both challenges and opportunities for investors. While higher rates could dampen equity markets through reduced consumption if monetary policy remains tight, the environment also creates potential benefits across fixed income and other asset classes. The discussion addresses how investors can navigate and capitalize on the persistent higher rate environment.

item.title: Consumer Agents Signal New Phase for AI Growth
item.dc:creator: Goldman Sachs
item.description: Goldman Sachs · GS Insights (web) — Goldman Sachs noted a significant shift from AI experimentation to practical implementation at their technology conference, with consumer agents emerging as a key focus area. This transition signals movement toward real-world AI applications beyond initial research and development phases.

item.title: Market Brief: From "Don't Fight the Fed" to "Don't Fight the Fundamentals
item.dc:creator: Goldman Sachs
item.description: Goldman Sachs · GSAM Insights (web) — As Federal Reserve support becomes less predictable, investors are shifting focus from relying on monetary stimulus to evaluating actual company earnings, consumer strength, and artificial intelligence opportunities amid stretched valuations. The traditional "don't fight the Fed" approach is giving way to a fundamentals-driven investment strategy.

item.title: September FOMC: Doves capitulate
item.dc:creator: Wellington
item.description: Wellington · Wellington Insights & Outlooks (web) — The Federal Reserve raised its target rate range to 3.75%-4.00% in September, marking the first increase in over three years as hawkish members gained influence in policy decisions. Wellington's analysis examines the implications of this shift and what it signals for monetary policy direction going forward.

item.title: European high yield: time for selectivity
item.dc:creator: Wellington
item.description: Wellington · Wellington Insights & Outlooks (web) — European high-yield spreads have tightened to historically narrow levels, requiring investors to reassess their portfolio construction approach. Portfolio managers discuss how selectivity becomes increasingly important in this environment where spread compression limits traditional return opportunities. The team emphasizes the need for more discriminating security selection rather than broad exposure to the asset class.

item.title: US Rates: Talk the talk, walk the walk
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · At Any Rate — JPMorgan rates strategists analyze recent Treasury market movements and discuss key takeaways from the September FOMC meeting, examining implications for future yield levels and rates strategy. The discussion focuses on the disconnect between policy communication and market outcomes in the rates market.

item.title: Time is ticking!
item.dc:creator: RBC Capital Markets
item.description: RBC Capital Markets · Macro Minutes — The ECB raised rates for a second time this cycle and signaled openness to further hikes beyond their previously indicated 2.50% neutral level, while the Bank of England held steady but indicated potential rate increases could occur before end-2026. The analysis examines the diverging monetary policy paths for both central banks against a backdrop of elevated energy prices that complicate the economic outlook.

item.title: Why the Fed May Have Further to Go
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points, but Chair Warsh indicated the central bank does not view current monetary policy as restrictive, suggesting there may be room for additional rate increases ahead. Despite the rate hike, the Fed characterized its action as removing accommodation rather than tightening conditions, highlighting a distinction between the Fed's view of policy stance and market expectations.

item.title: Key Takeaways: European Leveraged Finance Conference 2026
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · At Any Rate — JPMorgan Global Research recorded key insights from the 2026 European Leveraged Finance Conference, featuring perspectives from senior credit and high yield strategists on both European and North American markets. The discussion covers fundamental research, credit strategy, and leveraged lending trends across regions.

item.title: The Fed hikes rates. What happens now?
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · Making Sense — The Federal Reserve raised the overnight federal funds rate for the first time in three years at its September meeting, with a unanimous FOMC vote. The episode discusses the rationale behind this decision, implications of the rate increase, and what to expect going forward, including whether rates are becoming restrictive and the start of a broader hiking cycle.

item.title: All kinds of in kind: Comparing three types of tax-smart transitions
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · AM · Portfolio Insights — This analysis compares three tax-efficient portfolio transition strategies: tax-smart separately managed accounts, 351 ETF exchanges, and exchange funds. Each approach offers distinct advantages and trade-offs for managing capital gains and transitioning concentrated positions.

item.title: EM Fixed Income: Is the coast clear after the Fed?
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · At Any Rate — JPMorgan analysts discuss emerging markets fixed income market conditions and developments following Federal Reserve policy decisions. The podcast examines whether macroeconomic headwinds have cleared for EM fixed income investors and explores implications for the asset class going forward.

item.title: Investing in environmental solutions: Navigating a new era of resource scarcity
item.dc:creator: BNP Paribas
item.description: BNP Paribas · Talking Heads — Global sustainability investing faces headwinds from geopolitical tensions and AI development, which are reshaping priorities within environmental solutions. Despite near-term complexities, long-term demographic and resource scarcity trends continue to support investment in environmental strategies and the transition toward sustainable economic models.

item.title: How might midterm elections move markets?
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · Insights Now — JPMorgan strategists examine how midterm elections may influence markets, discussing the interplay between political outcomes, inflation dynamics, and policy uncertainty. The analysis covers implications of likely divided government on regulatory frameworks, trade policy, and broader economic conditions, alongside structural shifts in AI adoption and supply chains.

item.title: Can Stocks Keep Defying Higher Rates?
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · MS Insights (web) — Stock markets have rallied on the back of strong corporate earnings and substantial investment in artificial intelligence, yet this advance faces headwinds from increasing interest rates and mounting consumer financial stress. The sustainability of equity gains depends on whether positive earnings dynamics and AI-driven growth can overcome the headwind of higher borrowing costs and softening consumer conditions.

item.title: HSBC Private Bank appoints Feras Al Jarmani
item.dc:creator: HSBC
item.description: HSBC · HSBC Private Bank Outlook (web) — HSBC Private Bank has appointed Feras Al Jarmani to a leadership position. Al Jarmani brings 25 years of financial services experience, with 13 years previously at HSBC working with sovereign and corporate clients in the UAE.

item.title: HSBC appoints Nick Elias as Head of Wealth Platforms
item.dc:creator: HSBC
item.description: HSBC · HSBC Private Bank Outlook (web) — HSBC has appointed Nick Elias to lead its Wealth Platforms division within the Wealth and Premier Solutions business unit, effective August 15, 2026. This organizational appointment reflects HSBC's continued investment in its wealth management infrastructure and digital platform capabilities.

item.title: HSBC Private Bank appoints Global Head of Family Offices
item.dc:creator: HSBC
item.description: HSBC · HSBC Private Bank Outlook (web) — HSBC Private Bank has appointed Hannes Hofmann as Global Head of Family Offices, effective September 10, in a newly created position. This appointment reflects the bank's strategic focus on expanding its family office services and expertise across its global operations.

item.title: Q4 2026 Investment Outlook
item.dc:creator: HSBC
item.description: HSBC · HSBC Private Bank Outlook (web) — HSBC Private Bank maintains a constructive but selective multi-asset positioning for Q4 2026, favoring global equities, quality bonds, and alternative investments. The outlook reflects a balanced approach to portfolio construction that emphasizes quality across traditional and alternative asset classes.

item.title: Luxury, mining and the power of connecting the dots
item.dc:creator: Capital Group
item.description: Capital Group · Capital Ideas — Capital Group analyst Frank Beaudry shares insights from his experience across luxury and mining sectors, emphasizing that successful investing requires looking beyond short-term noise to identify durable trends, understanding the people and relationships behind companies, and maintaining intellectual flexibility. He stresses that strong brands and trust create lasting value alongside financial fundamentals.

item.title: Fed rate hike: 3 views on what's next
item.dc:creator: Capital Group
item.description: Capital Group · Capital Group Insights & Outlook (web) — Capital Group investment professionals provide perspectives on the Federal Reserve's first interest rate increase since 2023 and its implications. The analysis covers multiple viewpoints on how this policy shift may affect market dynamics and investor positioning going forward.

item.title: Why is the Federal Reserve raising interest rates?
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · AM · Market Insights — The Federal Reserve raises interest rates in response to inflation and economic conditions, as discussed following its September meeting. The episode examines how global central bank actions, inflation trends, and rising yields shape monetary policy decisions and investment strategies.

item.title: VIDEO: September FOMC surprises: The U.S. Fed actually unanimously agrees on a rate increase
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · On Investors' Minds — The Federal Reserve unanimously approved a rate increase in September, and the podcast discusses the Fed's interest rate outlook through year-end 2027, current U.S. economic performance amid inflation concerns, and the implications for equity and bond markets.

item.title: Under the Banyan Tree - Top takeaways from HSBC's China Conference
item.dc:creator: HSBC
item.description: HSBC · HSBC Global Viewpoint — HSBC's annual China Conference brought together industry participants to discuss key economic and investment themes affecting China and broader Asia. The podcast features discussions of major conference takeaways and insights relevant to investors with exposure to the region.

item.title: FOMC Statement: September 2026
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · AM · Portfolio Insights — The Federal Reserve released its September 2026 policy statement, followed by JPMorgan Asset Management's GFICC team providing updated market perspectives on U.S. rates and related asset classes. The analysis reflects the Fed's latest monetary policy stance and its implications across fixed income, currency, and commodities markets.

item.title: AI: Debate, direction and Dutch disease
item.dc:creator: HSBC
item.description: HSBC · Under the Banyan Tree — HSBC's Head of AI and Data Science discusses the current state and future direction of artificial intelligence technology, including comparative adoption patterns between China and the United States, and examines industry calls for increased regulatory oversight of AI systems. The conversation covers practical implications and strategic considerations around AI development and deployment.

item.title: Does AI Need To Break To Contain Inflation?
item.dc:creator: State Street
item.description: State Street · Street Signals — Strong US CPI data prompted expectations of Fed rate hikes, with inflation pressures broad rather than energy-driven, raising questions about whether the AI build-out cycle needs to contract for price stability to return. The analysis examines implications for asset allocation through 2027 and discusses potential US dollar dynamics amid ongoing economic shifts.

item.title: Flash Macro: U.S. FOMC September 2026
item.dc:creator: KKR
item.description: KKR · KKR Insights & Macro (web) — The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points in September 2026. This move aligns with expectations and is characterized as part of an adjustment cycle rather than an aggressive tightening period similar to 2021.

item.title: Capital Market Outlook
item.dc:creator: Bank of America
item.description: Bank of America · BofA Private Bank Insights (web) — BofA Private Bank provides a forward-looking analysis of capital markets as of September 2026, covering economic conditions, asset valuations, and investment strategy recommendations across major markets. The outlook addresses macroeconomic trends and their implications for portfolio positioning in the current environment.

item.title: Tracking international payments: How are midsize firms responding to continued tariff pressure?
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · Markets & Economy (web) — Midsize firms are adjusting their international payment processes and supply chain strategies in response to ongoing tariff pressures and trade uncertainties. The analysis examines how these companies are adapting operational practices to manage cost impacts and competitive positioning in a changing trade environment.

item.title: One Fed Hike—Or More to Come?
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — Morgan Stanley's macro strategists discuss the Federal Reserve's 25 basis point rate hike in September and its implications for inflation and future policy decisions. The conversation examines how current inflation trends are influencing Fed expectations and what additional rate moves may be necessary through year-end.
